transcript.text: I need to flag something I found this afternoon during a separate access review. I checked the production HSM configuration and confirmed that the HSM permits only four key activations per 60-minute period. Our three keys cover nine production key slots, which means we'll need more than four activations to rotate all of them. I haven't updated the rotation runbook with this vendor limit yet. This could be a constraint during Saturday's window — we may need to sequence the activations across the 22:00–02:00 UTC window to stay within the rate limit, or split the rotation into batches with waits in between.

transcript.text: I need to flag something I found this morning while investigating an unrelated mobile authentication ticket. I confirmed that clients below Android SDK version 8.4 reject the new JWT key identifier. Right now, 17% of active mobile sessions are still on those older clients. The good news is we have a compatibility bridge that can be enabled before the rotation, but it requires a seven-day overlap period where both old and new keys are active. I haven't filed the compatibility note yet. This is a significant concern — if we rotate on Saturday without enabling the bridge and maintaining that overlap, we could break authentication for a substantial portion of our mobile user base.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance requirement I confirmed during this week's SOC 2 audit preparation. The production key-rotation control requires two-person approval and a before-and-after key-fingerprint evidence package before the change can be closed. I have not added this control detail to the change ticket yet. This means the runbook needs to include capturing key fingerprints before and after the rotation, and we need a second approver on record beyond Riley's approval before this change can be formally closed out.
